roc-curve rocTable {\"truth\":\"Truth\",.subtitle: ROC curve analysis
roc-curve rocTable {\"truth\":\"Truth\",.notes: “1” is the positive class (N = 10); “0” is negative (N = 10). AUC is the Mann-Whitney U statistic divided by the product of the class sizes — identical to the trapezoidal area under the empirical ROC curve. An AUC of 0.5 is chance; 1 is perfect separation. The 95% confidence interval is DeLong's (DeLong et al. 1988), truncated to [0, 1] — the upper limit hit 1 and was truncated. The optimal cutpoint maximises Youden's J (sensitivity + specificity − 1); among tied J values the highest threshold is reported. Tied scores count 0.5 in the AUC, and a threshold equal to a tied score classifies the whole tie as positive. Uses complete pairs only; no rows were left out.
